briefs.headline: The long end is getting relief after Monday's 2002 highs: the 10Y is ≈5.28% (−3 bp) and the 30Y ≈5.63%, with Brent back under $100 and futures up 0.25–0.4%. Today's tests are the $58B 3Y auction at noon CT and Williams/Bowman, ahead of Wednesday's 10Y reopening and FOMC minutes.

OPEC+ held November output steady and the G7's 100M-barrel stock release has WTI under $90. That takes some pressure off the long end, with the 10Y ≈3 bp lower at ≈5.25%. But France's debt troubles pushed the euro to a 17-month low, and ISM services at 9:00 AM CT is the day's first test before $119B of 3Y/10Y/30Y supply.

The market is leaning bearish into $119B of 3Y/10Y/30Y supply and Wednesday's FOMC minutes. A +29K payrolls print moved the hike to December, but the 10Y still finished the week at 5.28%, the 2s10s curve steepened ≈20 bp, and Wall Street's gold survey turned net bearish for the first time in months.

A +29K payrolls miss pushed the Fed's next hike from October to December, but the 10Y still ended the week near 5.28%. That leaves next week's $119B of 3Y/10Y/30Y supply and Wednesday's FOMC minutes as the test of whether the long end can hold below Thursday's 5.344% high.

Payrolls at 7:30 AM CT (+84–90K est.) decide whether October hike odds (~28–36%) come back, while a possible diesel and crude stock release has knocked Brent back under $100 and the 10Y sits near 5.24%.

briefs.edition: Evening edition · prep for Fri Oct 2
briefs.headline: Soft August PCE cut October hike odds to about 35–38% and the 10-year faded from 5.34% to 5.24%, but December is priced near-certain; Friday's 7:30 AM CT payrolls (+90K est.) decides if October comes back.
